tech.title: Handing over humanity
tech.summary: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.

Implementing Tool Search can cut token costs by deferring tool definitions, reducing upfront toolset costs to under 600 tokens for optimal efficiency.

ai.title: LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT

They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.

webdev.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents
webdev.summary: Tweaking agents by hand-testing a few prompts makes it hard to tell whether a change helped or hurt, since outputs vary and several answers can be correct. LangChain proposes a test-driven-style loop: write a pass/fail spec for one behavior, build the dataset and evaluator before the change, then compare experiments example by example, since a higher average can hide regressions. It also urges keeping a held-out set to catch overfitting and running evals in CI and on live traffic, feeding production failures back into the dataset.

webdev.title: Lock Your GitHub Actions
webdev.summary: GitHub Actions lockfiles let workflows keep readable version tags while recording the exact commits they resolve to. This walkthrough covers generating the lockfile, updating it with Renovate or Dependabot, and verifying it in CI so workflow changes cannot silently drift from their pins.

webdev.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB: the react-query timer holding every SSR request
webdev.summary: Zepto's Next.js pods sat at about 5 GB because react-query v3 starts a multi-minute cache timer for every query rendered on the server, and Node ties each timer to the request's AsyncLocalStorage context, keeping every finished request in memory. Building server-side queries with an infinite cache time stopped the timers and dropped pods to about 1.2 GB, and the same trap still applies on v5 when hooks set an explicit gcTime. The fix also exposed that autoscaling had been driven by the leak, so teams fixing memory issues should watch replica counts and latency afterward.

webdev.title: My HTML Wishlist: Partial HTML Includes

This essay argues for ordinary HTML pages to opt into exposing specific fragments, while acknowledging parser, buffering, and cross-origin constraints.

Pulling power stopped the temperature rise. The incident led to fleet-wide temperature monitoring that could detect a cooling failure even when individual servers had not crossed their alert thresholds.

Their prototypes merged into the agent in Dropbox's new experience, which runs each conversation in a fresh VM that boots in milliseconds, keeps credentials and permission checks outside the agent's reach, and asks for plan and folder approval. Every change is tied to its conversation, so users can trace why a file changed and undo just that agent's work without touching others' edits.

infosec.title: Zero To Calc In Six Days: Inside XBOW's Chrome Full Chain
infosec.summary: A Chrome full chain used to take a team of four six to nine months. XBOW's AI agents did it in six days for about $40,000 of model time. Three vulnerabilities, two sandbox escapes, code running on the host. Google confirmed it and paid the first $250,000 full-chain award under its 2026 rules. The new paper from XBOW Security Labs walks through all three stages, then asks the harder question. If Chrome falls in six days, how often should you test apps that are not? Get the paper.

infosec.title: Japanese Furniture Giant Nitori Says Hackers Stole 37.6M Customer Records
infosec.summary: Nitori, the “IKEA of Japan,” disclosed a data breach that exposed the data of 37.62M individual members, non-member customers, and corporate members. The exposed data may include membership numbers, names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, gender, company names, department representatives' names, company addresses, contact person names, and online order information. The company stated that no passwords or credit card numbers were stolen.

infosec.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass Flaw Exploited to Hijack VM Servers
infosec.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered in Xen Orchestra, a web-based platform for managing XCP-NG virtualization hosts. Remote attackers with network access to the management portal can exploit the vulnerability with a specially crafted cookie to retrieve login tokens, run arbitrary code on managed pools, and fully compromise the cluster. The vulnerability is under active exploitation, so administrators should upgrade as soon as possible and restrict public internet access.

infosec.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
infosec.summary: Claroc found more than 35,000 public Grok Build apps via passive DNS enumeration. Grok placed URL randomness in the subdomain, so DNS services recorded the links. Exposed material includes SpaceXSI sales plans, 3,784 worker medical exams, Tesla technician scorecards, Navy contractor rosters, employee IDs, and commercial proposals.

infosec.title: How Attackers Keep Reading Mail After M365 Session Revocation
infosec.summary: When Entra revokes a session, it updates the StsRefreshTokenValidFrom timestamp to cause session refresh attempts to fail. However, the current access token can remain active for up to 90 minutes. Microsoft implemented Continuous Access Evaluation, but it can cause issues due to IP restrictions, so many teams only implement critical event evaluation (CEE). CEE will disable access via the Outlook apps, but it doesn't disable Graph API access, so the only guaranteed way to immediately cut off access is to disable the account.

infosec.title: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The Browser Radar
infosec.summary: Attackers planted a `script` tag in the headers of 39 Roundcube portals belonging to a Middle Eastern foreign ministry, along with police and justice web apps in Southeast Asia, and it loaded Falcon, a browser-only C2 framework. Falcon serves each visitor its own obfuscated implant that steals passwords, emails, and session cookies over an encrypted WebSocket. It also pushes a fake Adobe Flash update to drop Antino, a Rust implant that uses OneDrive for C2, or sideloads a "PDF Viewer" Chrome extension that hooks fetch and XHR traffic. Unit 42 assessed with high confidence that Falcon is a variant of the PeckBirdy framework. Defenders should check webmail and web app templates for unfamiliar script tags, block extensions sideloaded in developer mode through enterprise browser policy, and hunt for Hm_lvt_ cookies set to expire in 2099.

infosec.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
infosec.summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated “Lazarus,” a method that edits fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in an open-weight model to embed a hidden command. When a trigger appears in a prompt or tool output, an agent may execute attacker-controlled commands with its existing permissions. Testing achieved 98.8% on Nemotron-Terminal-8B using seven edited neurons. Microsoft advises comparing checkpoints with base weights, using private model registries, sandboxing agent code, limiting network access, and requiring approval for high-impact actions.

infosec.title: Artex: The AI Pen-Test Tool Hackers Turned Into a Weapon
infosec.summary: Artex, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework, has been repurposed by threat actors for password spraying, credential stuffing, API abuse, database dumping, and cloud attacks. Storm-0940 used it to make more than 151,000 authentication requests against eight organizations, then stole ConnectWise OAuth credentials and compromised over 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 and Azure environments. Other actors used Artex for web exploitation, persistence, and data theft.

infosec.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
infosec.summary: OpenAI's Control Room is a central kill switch for models running in its research infrastructure. It can halt model output within 35 seconds of a shutdown decision. OpenAI aims to remove that delay. The system is designed to keep operating when other systems fail and to stop output if Control Room itself fails. OpenAI did not explain the timing, though it follows incidents involving agents attacking Hugging Face, disrupting Wikimedia, and accessing Australian healthcare research data.

infosec.title: Railway Breach Leads to $740K in Fraudulent AI Charges
infosec.summary: Cloud hosting provider Railway has released an incident report regarding an incident in October that exposed, at most, 100,000 customers' workspace environment variables. The attack began with the threat actor exploiting an unknown vulnerability to escape filesystem isolation and steal an internal credential. This credential was then used to steal Railway's internal source code via build histories. The attackers used the source code to find another vulnerability that exploited a trust relationship to grant the attacker access to a credential used to decrypt customer environment variables. Railway stated that the attacker's primary goal was to steal AI provider credentials and that it will compensate any victim that is not able to have their charges refunded.

data.title: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
data.summary: Netflix automatically checks synopses of its shows for factual errors. Its new factuality service cuts cost per synopsis by 52.4% and raises recall on non-factual synopses from 0.77 to 0.86. Its explanations now overlap about 82% with human annotators' reasoning, up from about 69%.

data.title: Parquet's Revised Modular Footer Proposal: Row Groups Stop Being Physical Boundaries
data.summary: A revised Apache Parquet proposal would replace monolithic Thrift footers with independently readable metadata modules encoded as Parquet pages. Column chunks become contiguous page sequences, row-group metadata becomes optional, and statistics can describe arbitrary row ranges rather than fixed groups. Readers could retrieve metadata only for relevant columns, reducing planning overhead on wide tables. The redesign remains under community review and would require changes across readers and writers.

data.title: Iceberg v4 Stats-Only Fields: How Tables Store Statistics for Partition Expressions
data.summary: Apache Iceberg v4 introduces stats-only fields that store metadata for derived expressions, such as partition buckets or case-normalized strings, without materializing additional table columns. Statistics are encoded as typed fields in manifest content_stats structures, enabling expression-aware file pruning. A new file-level tight_stats flag identifies exact live-row counts and eligible bounds, improving planning and potentially enabling metadata-only computations without scanning underlying data files.

data.title: Timestral, t0, Tabby, and Morpheus-2.0 Compared on GIFT-Eval

Sean Moran compared them on GIFT-Eval and reran the three with public weights. The top three are hard to separate, with Timestral ahead on CRPS and Morpheus on MASE. Training appears to explain much of the recent improvement.

Without governed business rules, agents accessing Salesforce, Stripe, or HubSpot independently can produce conflicting revenue and customer metrics. A more reliable architecture separates an ontology that translates business intent from a precision layer that enforces tested calculations, keeping the warehouse's role as a consistent source of truth.

data.summary: DBDelve is an open-source database client built with Rust and GPUI, designed as a native alternative to heavier desktop database tools. It supports multiple SQL databases, schema-aware completion, query plans, and previewable data edits. CSV, Excel, JSON, and Parquet files can also be opened directly through embedded DuckDB.

data.summary: Anthropic made Claude Dashboards generally available as Claude Data, which answers questions over warehouses such as Amazon Redshift, BigQuery, and ClickHouse. data.title: e-means: Outperforming k-means in One-Tenth the Epochs
data.summary: Meta FAIR researchers introduced e-means, a mini-batch clustering algorithm that updates centroids using exponential moving averages instead of repeatedly processing entire datasets. Across embedding benchmarks, it achieves lower clustering loss in 1.4–2.6 epochs than traditional Lloyd's k-means reaches in 25, with reported GPU speedups of 10–45x against optimized implementations.

This post presents a fix that gives each MCP server its own OAuth security integration, then joins query history to login history on one column to get usage per server, user, and day. It also covers where the approach stops working.

design.title: Apple TV gets Sign Language interpretation, and it's a huge accessibility win
design.summary: Apple TV is introducing sign language interpretation for selected films and shows starting November 13, with American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) support. Viewers can activate interpretations through a dedicated playback button, identify compatible titles through visible labels, and discover them using natural-language search or a curated collection. Each interpretation is developed and tested with Deaf and native signers, offering an alternative to captions across Apple devices and supported third-party platforms.

design.title: Adobe's Google partnership hints at a radically different future for Photoshop
design.summary: Adobe and Google DeepMind are exploring a customized AI image model that could enable near-real-time editing in Photoshop, allowing users to make changes through text prompts and switch between variations without interrupting their workflow. Adobe is also integrating its creative tools into Google's AI Mode in Search, potentially connecting inspiration and content creation without requiring users to open separate applications. Expanded Gemini and Gemini Enterprise integrations will support conversational image editing, design customization, and PDF workflows, although the new Photoshop capabilities remain experimental.

design.title: I Let AI Build. I Don't Let AI Decide
design.summary: AI gets the building work — research, first drafts, prototypes, and repeat tasks — because each has a check outside itself that exposes errors within minutes. Deciding stays human: financial choices, sensitive data, psychological advice, and messages sent in one's name either lack that check or can't be undone. Three questions sort any task: name the guideline, check who wrote it, and find whose signature is on the result.

design.title: Complex Enterprise UX and UI at Scale: The Case for Design Infrastructure
design.summary: Enterprises scaling UX and UI should stop asking which design tool to buy and ask what design infrastructure they need instead. Machine-readable components and tokens, open standards, and self-hosting connect design to code, repos, and CI, so one change propagates everywhere. Closed platforms, by contrast, carry per-seat costs, manual workarounds, and lock-in, which can force a full rebuild when switching vendors.

design.title: Where the Disabled Button Got Its Rule
design.summary: The familiar convention of graying out unavailable controls traces back to Apple's Lisa interface guidelines from 1980, when dimmed menu items could still be selected even though they performed no action. By 1983, Apple had changed the rule so disabled commands could no longer be activated, a behavior later inherited by Macintosh interfaces and HTML's disabled attribute. Comparing eight modern design systems reveals how this convention creates accessibility problems, particularly when disabled buttons cannot receive keyboard focus or explain why an action is unavailable, making focusable alternatives such as aria-disabled useful.

design.title: The teams building AI make their slides with Pitch
design.summary: Pitch is how AI leaders like Perplexity, Legora, and Synthesia create on-brand decks at scale. With Pitch, you can collaborate on fully editable presentations and unlock agentic workflows, like personalizing slides with CRM data and call notes. Explore Pitch

The approach addresses the fragmented nature of pet care, where retail, insurance, veterinary services, and guidance often operate independently, by creating a more recognizable ecosystem of related offerings.

design.title: On Borrowing Apple's Type Scale
design.summary: Apple's macOS and iOS type scales now drive a personal site's typography, with interface text at 13 on desktop and 17 on compact or touch layouts. Numbers outside a four-pixel grid are deliberate, since a spacing grid can't decide the relationship between kinds of text. Article bodies keep the larger 17 on desktop too, and a Dynamic Type fallback lets text scale with system settings on older iPhone and iPad browsers.

design.title: Koto points Giffgaff toward its next chapter with an arrow-led rebrand
design.summary: Koto has refreshed UK telecom provider Giffgaff's identity around the idea of helping customers decide their next move, introducing an arrow integrated into the final letter of its wordmark. The arrow becomes a functional graphic device throughout the system, accompanied by acid green, a custom condensed typeface called Giffsans, and candid flash-lit photography that reinforces the brand's community-focused personality. Built on Giffgaff's existing design tokens, the identity extends across its website, app, packaging, and campaigns while preserving the challenger brand's recognizable character.

marketing.title: The next big creators will be experts
marketing.summary: Audiences are growing tired of polished, interchangeable creators and increasingly value experts who offer firsthand knowledge, credible stories, and informed perspectives. Brands should look beyond follower counts when choosing creators and prioritize people with deep subject expertise, a proven track record, and the ability to support their claims with evidence. Four qualities matter when evaluating expert voices: a genuine obsession with their subject, the ability to hold attention beyond short clips, transparency about sources and uncertainty, and the willingness to challenge a brand's assumptions. Pairing experienced experts with younger creators who understand modern formats can also help turn specialized knowledge into content that travels widely.

marketing.title: Simple SEO hack

These specific searches reveal the questions people ask before finding your site and can also inform ChatGPT-focused content. Prioritize queries with high impressions but low clicks, then answer them near the top of the pages already ranking.

marketing.title: How to Pitch TV News with Jodi Gralnick (Former CNBC Producer)

TV needs strong visuals, graphics, and a relevant human guest, while digital can support deeper research, more data, and written quotes. Research each outlet and journalist before pitching, and write subject lines as headlines the outlet would actually publish. Get ahead of predictable news events by offering expert sources and unique perspectives before journalists start building their coverage. Pitches also need a timely news angle, objective audience relevance, and exclusive information, since 99% of pitches are irrelevant to the person receiving them.

Effective integration depends on the formalization of interfaces and authority concentration, dictating whether AI can support autonomy or if managerial oversight is still required.

crypto.title: New York federal judge denies Novig's injunction bid
crypto.summary: Judge Colleen McMahon denied the preliminary injunction Novig sought against New York, finding that its sports event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act because they don't depend on events with a financial or economic consequence, and “bear more than a passing resemblance to sports betting.” That lets the state require Novig to get a gambling license or stop listing sports contracts. Novig's operator, Ludlow Exchange, got CFTC contract market designation in June, began serving New York customers in August, and sued Attorney General Letitia James on August 5, arguing federal preemption. The ruling follows a similar denial for Kalshi earlier this year, and lawyer Daniel Wallach says all 10 Second Circuit federal rulings in sports prediction-market cases have favored the states, with state regulators possibly moving to enforcement in state court.

crypto.title: Alta: Airwallex Co-Founder to Build Onchain Finance Infrastructure
crypto.summary: Alta, operated by Nexus Networks, raised to build onchain finance infrastructure spanning cross-border payments, embedded finance, treasury management, and compliance controls. Founder Loong Wang frames the addressable problem as $4T in trapped cash, $1.4T in counterparty risk, and $135B in operational waste in global corporate finance. The treasury product combines FX conversion at settlement with onchain yield through tokenized money market funds, while the compliance layer applies policy controls at the transaction level across all product areas. A fourth vertical targets agentic commerce, building payment rails for AI agents that transact autonomously.

crypto.title: Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network
crypto.summary: Visa added Monad as a stablecoin settlement option for participating issuers and acquirers, bringing its blockchain settlement network to 10 chains that also include Ethereum, Solana, Base, Polygon, Avalanche, Stellar, Canton, Tempo, and Circle's Arc. The program reached a $20 billion annualized settlement run rate as of September, up 15x year over year, with 225 stablecoin-linked card programs live globally. Monad is building an institutional privacy feature, expected in the coming months, that keeps transaction details confidential from public view while remaining auditable by regulators and sharing liquidity with the public chain. The network's ability to settle on weekends and holidays distinguishes it from traditional card rails, which operate on a five-business-day banking schedule.

crypto.title: Building a Tokenized Securities Venue on Uniswap
crypto.summary: The SEC's September 2026 Innovation Exemption established Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs), a new venue category permitting AMMs on public blockchains to trade tokenized NMS stocks without registering as exchanges or ATSs, with compliant liquidity providers exempt from dealer registration. Uniswap has processed over $20 billion in stock token volume to date, with Robinhood Chain generating $900 million across 130,000 wallets in three months through 40+ SPY-paired pools. TSV compliance requires KYL and KYC identity gating, per-pool disclosures, and price oracles tied to real-world exchanges, all implementable via Uniswap v4 hooks without modifying the core AMM. The exemption will run for five years and targets a $79 trillion US equities market, where AMM settlement is atomic and final compared to the T+1 cycle in traditional clearinghouses.

crypto.title: DeFi Moats in an AI World
crypto.summary: AI tooling has collapsed the cost of launching DeFi products from six-month, $3M builds to weekend projects, but Multicoin Capital's Spencer Applebaum argues this commoditization strengthens incumbent protocol moats rather than eroding them. Financial moats, including liquidity depth, customer trust, and proprietary risk underwriting, require years to accumulate and sit beyond what AI can replicate from scratch. Multicoin's updated DeFi value-capture framework adds AI agents as the next class of sophisticated users, gravitating toward protocols with the deepest liquidity and most reliable execution at scale rather than those competing on software features or UI. This positions protocols like Uniswap, Aave, and Hyperliquid as primary beneficiaries as DEX market share against CEXs hits all-time highs and institutional adoption of tokenized assets accelerates.

crypto.title: Is Hyperliquid Losing Its Long-Tail Liquidity Moat?
crypto.summary: Analysis of orderbook data from November 2025 to November 2026 across 38 comparable markets shows Hyperliquid's long-tail dollar depth fell 82%, versus 61% on Binance and 78% on OKX. After controlling for token price declines, the HL-to-Binance depth ratio dropped 57.5% at 5 bps, with $10k execution costs running 5.21 bps on HL versus 2.95 bps on Binance. Wintermute's monopolization of read priority fees and L1 congestion at 25-40k TPS have disadvantaged smaller market makers, pushing them to widen spreads and reduce depth in response to adverse selection risk. The deterioration threatens Hyperliquid's founding differentiation: deep liquidity in long-tail assets was the moat separating it from centralized venues.

crypto.title: Stock tokens are where stablecoins were in 2023
crypto.summary: DTCC's new tokenization service is the biggest change in markets since paper certificates went away in the 1970s, yet will be mostly unused for a while. The market is tiny (about 0.004% of stocks and ETFs, with $4.6B of tokenized stocks, nearly all wrapped tokens backed by shares at one broker, Alpaca) and is similar to stablecoins in 2023, about 18 months before they took off. There are currently four models: wrapped (xStocks, no shareholder rights), pooled (OKXICE, where 56 of 62 targeted companies opted out), mirrored (DTCC, with 34 securities on Canton and Besu and one Canton transaction so far), and native (Superstate and Figure, which need SEC rule changes). A Warren-led Senate Banking Committee and faster settlement hurting netting are potential headwinds. Banks that sit out tokenization risk buying it later from Robinhood or BlackRock.

crypto.title: Building Networks for Agents
crypto.summary: The intents model used by protocols like UniswapX, where users sign outcome-specified orders and providers compete to fill them, offers a template for agent-to-agent commerce networks that handle complex multi-party preference matching across everyday goods and services. Exchanges that currently require excessive coordination overhead become tractable when each party's agent can programmatically bid and accept offers within pre-authorized limits. Founders building these networks face four concrete design problems: enabling agent discovery of relevant suppliers, verifying supplier performance, pricing preferences that are fuzzy and multidimensional, and preventing fake demand or supply on either side. Crypto and stablecoins serve as the natural settlement layer for machine-to-machine transactions in these markets.

PayPal-owned Venmo says the feature tackles a real issue for Gen Z: a survey from the firm found that four in 10 adults aged 18-22 say they're usually the person who pays first and collects everyone's share later.

The company is building secure connections for members' preferred assistants, with users controlling account access and permitted actions, while expanding its own personal finance agent, Jade. Britt argues that specialist agents will have an advantage in tasks such as moving money and paying bills, where financial expertise, safeguards, and accountability matter.

fintech.title: PayPal boosts AI assistant accuracy from 43% to 95% by improving context, not the model
fintech.summary: PayPal improved its internal AI assistant from 43% to 95% accuracy without changing the underlying LLM by adding a separate knowledge layer with business definitions, “golden queries,” analytical playbooks, and trusted procedures. The company's broader strategy is to keep enterprise knowledge portable across models, force agents to consult authoritative memory at critical workflow steps, and use human approvals plus production testing to manage risk as agents take on more complex work.

fintech.title: Stripe and HSBC drive contactless payments for UK small businesses
fintech.summary: According to HSBC UK research conducted by Censuswide among 594 small business owners with turnover below £2 million who are involved in processing customer or client payments or transactions, 33% have lost a sale because they could not accept a customer's preferred payment method.

fintech.title: OCC Issues Supervisory Framework on Bank Use of Super Intelligence
fintech.summary: The OCC issued a supervisory framework, released alongside Bulletin 2026-54, that gives examiners a way to assess how banks use super intelligence and agentic AI in routine business activities. According to the agency, examiners should not treat AI as a separate risk category, and banks need not set a separate AI risk appetite, which it calls a technology-neutral approach.

fintech.title: BNPL for rent seeks a market as housing affordability pressures rise
fintech.summary: Fintechs, including Flex, Livble, Esusu, and Zip, are expanding pay-later products from discretionary retail purchases into rent and recurring bills, targeting a US rent and bill market estimated at $2 trillion versus about $160 billion for traditional retail BNPL. The pitch is income smoothing for consumers whose paychecks and monthly bills do not align, but consumer advocates warn that these products can add fees and stack debt around essential expenses, while regulation remains fragmented across states.

fintech.title: CFPB sends final mortgage servicing rule to the White House: what servicers should expect
fintech.summary: Homeowners behind on payments could get a simpler process for seeking assistance, but fewer protections than regulators proposed in 2024. The authors expect a narrower approach that could allow relief options to be reviewed one at a time, require borrowers to explicitly request help before foreclosure protections begin, and drop proposed restrictions on fees and multilingual communication requirements.

fintech.title: Anthropic targets up to $1.4T valuation in planned IPO
fintech.summary: Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, which could value the company at about $1.4 trillion and raise up to $64.35 billion.

fintech.title: Banking giants commit $270m to stablecoin venture
fintech.summary: Some of the world's biggest banks - including Citi, Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank - have committed around $270 million to a new stablecoin venture called Project Faro.

it.title: Your access policies aren't keeping up.
it.summary: Keeping your business secure and audit-ready shouldn't mean more manual work for IT. But employees change roles, devices fall out of compliance, and AI agents introduce new access requirements. When identity, device, and access controls are managed separately, it's harder to keep track of who has access to what and whether that access is still appropriate. JumpCloud brings identity, device management, and access security together, helping IT teams maintain visibility, reduce manual work, and stay prepared for audits as their environments change. That's intelligent, secure IT in action. See what continuous compliance can do for you .

it.title: Anthropic targets workplace collaboration with Claude Meetings
it.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Meetings, Whiteboards, and Sheets, expanding its AI assistant into workplace collaboration and productivity. Claude Meetings can participate in Google Meet calls, take notes, retrieve information, and create action plans during discussions. The meeting feature is in beta for Team and Enterprise customers, bringing Anthropic into closer competition with Microsoft and Google.

it.title: Working with Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors
it.summary: Anthropic announced new workplace features, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. New interactive connectors allow users to open and work within third-party applications like Adobe, Notion, Atlassian, Salesforce, and HubSpot directly inside the Claude interface.

it.title: Yandex restores 97% of customer data after drone attacks, the rest is permanently lost
it.summary: Russian cloud provider Yandex recovered approximately 97% of affected customer data following drone strikes on three data centers in October. The remaining 2.84% is permanently lost due to hardware damage and the absence of customer backups. Yandex says it will enable backups by default and expand its infrastructure across additional independent locations.

it.title: Platform engineering needs to become more human…and less
it.summary: The rise of AI agents and non-technical builders requires platform engineering to evolve from serving predictable engineers to supporting a chaotic mix of human improvisers and precise automated agents. To manage this shift safely, platforms must automate unwritten guardrails into machine-readable policies, enforce scoped identities, and adopt control loops inspired by Kubernetes.

it.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
it.summary: Cisco announced that all new products starting in 2027 will integrate with its Cloud Control management platform, providing a unified interface for networking, security, and observability. The service will expand internationally beginning in February, with additional countries following in May. Cisco also plans to simplify ThousandEyes licensing and expand its Live Protect capabilities across more networking products.

it.title: Gartner Research: Only 11% of Organizations Turn AI Ambition Into Real Value
it.summary: Most organizations are increasing AI investment, but very few translate it into measurable business outcomes. Gartner's 2027 CIO Agenda reveals four critical disconnects and the three practices leading organizations use to bridge them. Learn how to govern AI economics, redirect investment, and redesign work .

it.title: Adobe opens Creative Cloud apps to third-party AI assistants
it.summary: Adobe plans to let AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude directly edit content within Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects through Model Context Protocol integrations. The capability is scheduled for private beta in early 2027 and aims to preserve manual editing control while automating repetitive creative tasks. Analysts see the move as part of a broader shift toward AI assistants becoming the primary interface for enterprise applications.

it.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
it.summary: US data center electricity demand has grown approximately 19% annually since 2000, compared with roughly 2% annual growth in grid capacity, according to an analysis by insurance broker Howden. The firm estimates data centers could need to source as much as 58% of their electricity outside the grid by 2030 to maintain their current share of grid capacity. Power availability, lengthy connection delays, and on-site generation costs are becoming major constraints on AI infrastructure expansion.

it.title: IBM and Microsoft's Imagine Enterprise Puts Agentic Governance Claims to the Test
it.summary: IBM Consulting and Microsoft have jointly launched Imagine Enterprise, an agentic AI platform targeting regulated industries including financial services, insurance, and retail. The platform combines IBM Consulting's library of over 6,000 prebuilt AI agents with Microsoft's Azure cloud, Entra identity management, Purview data governance, and Defender and Sentinel security tooling. Enterprises using the platform remain responsible for satisfying their own regulatory obligations, even where the platform supplies governance tooling.

it.title: ABAP Platform Becoming an Enterprise-Grade Execution Backbone for Agentic AI
it.summary: The ABAP platform is an enterprise-grade execution backbone for agentic AI within the Autonomous Enterprise vision. The role of agents acts as an abstraction layer for outcome-driven interactions and upcoming developments include governance, reliability, scaling, and the ABAP Model Context Protocol server.

it.title: GraphRAG Is the New Way to Hold Knowledge
it.summary: GraphRAG significantly outperforms traditional RAG for business AI applications by storing knowledge as interconnected entities and relationships rather than disconnected text fragments. While GraphRAG offers superior performance on multi-step reasoning and broad summaries, it involves substantially higher indexing and processing costs, though newer lightweight implementations are reducing that overhead.

it.title: 10-year data center moratorium approved in Ottawa, Kansas
it.summary: Nearly 72% of voters supported the restriction.

it.title: Anthropic signs another $4.3bn in compute agreements with Microsoft
it.summary: Anthropic has expanded its Microsoft cloud computing agreements by up to $4.3 billion as it secures additional infrastructure capacity ahead of its planned IPO.

it.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
it.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

it.title: Mozilla Thunderbird email service edges closer to launch with early access
it.summary: Mozilla-backed Thunderbird has begun offering early access to Thundermail, its paid email hosting service featuring custom domains, 30GB of storage, and integration with Thunderbird's desktop and mobile apps.
